title: Internal and sectionwise module operations agree
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For each scheme $T$ use the small pro-étale site with its universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the sheafified tensor product of abelian sheaves [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], the pulled-back ring object $\Lambda_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and its reconstructed section-ring sheaf $B_T$. Let
$$E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathrm{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$$
be the canonical equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Write $f^*_{\rm int},f_{*,\rm int}$ for the internal module functors and their specified adjunction [def-sfb-module-upper-star], [def-sfb-module-lower-star], [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. For $f:T'\to T$ let $f^*_{\rm sec},f_{*,\rm sec}$ be the sectionwise ringed-topos functors for the ring isomorphism $f^{-1}B_T\cong B_{T'}$ induced by $\alpha_f$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]: pullback is $B_{T'}\otimes_{f^{-1}B_T}f^{-1}(-)$ (sheafified sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and direct image is ordinary sheaf direct image with scalar restriction along the adjunct $B_T\to f_*B_{T'}$, with their canonical adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Then the canonical comparisons give
$$E_{T'}f^*_{\rm int}\cong f^*_{\rm sec}E_T,\qquad E_Tf_{*,\rm int}\cong f_{*,\rm sec}E_{T'},$$
and identify the specified internal adjunction with the sectionwise ringed-topos adjunction, including its unit and counit. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, write $j_{!,\rm int}$ for [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and $j_{!,\rm sec}$ for the sectionwise extension by zero, the left adjoint to $j^*_{\rm sec}$. There is a canonical comparison
$$E_Tj_{!,\rm int}\cong j_{!,\rm sec}E_U$$
identifying these open adjunctions. In a cartesian square of schemes with open vertical immersions and compatible pulled-back coefficients, these comparisons identify the internal open-extension base-change transformation with the sectionwise one (the transformation defined as the adjunction mate of the pullback-composition comparison). Thus whenever that sectionwise transformation is invertible, so is the internal one. The equivalences $E_T$ are additive exact equivalences, so exactness and exact sequences of these operations transport between the two module categories.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-section-ring-lax-pushforward-coherence] to each small pro-étale site and $R_T=\Lambda_T$. It gives additive exact $E_T$ and inverse, so both preserve and reflect exact sequences. The universe and tensor hypotheses are precisely those fixed in the statement.

source.place: Steps 1–2, internal/sectionwise operation transport; assembly step 1 from the two extracted coherence statements.

proof.text: For $f:T\prime\to T$, use its continuous site pullback and $\psi=\eta_f=f_*\alpha_f\circ\eta_f^{\rm Ab}$, a ring-object map by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. By [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal] its prescribed lax structure has the sheafification-unit normalization. The pushforward definition is $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta_f}\operatorname{mapMod}(f_*^{\rm Ab})$. The reconstruction lemma gives the required ring adjunct on sections and the identity-on-sheaves comparison $r_f:E_Tf_{*,\rm int}\cong f_{*,\rm sec}E_{T\prime}$.

source.place: Steps 1–2, internal/sectionwise operation transport; assembly step 2 from the two extracted coherence statements.

proof.text: The two specified pullback/direct-image adjunctions exist by [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-equivalence-square-inverse-mate-coherence] to $r_f$: its normalized comparison $c_f$ identifies the full Hom bijections, unit and counit. Apply that clause again to $j_{!,\rm int}\dashv j^*_{\rm int}$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], the sectionwise open adjunction and right comparison $c_j$, obtaining $o_j:E_Tj_{!,\rm int}\cong j_{!,\rm sec}E_U$ with the same normalization.

source.place: Steps 1–2, internal/sectionwise operation transport; assembly step 3 from the two extracted coherence statements.

proof.text: For composable $f:T''\to T'$, $g:T'\to T$, the base-change site functor of $g\circ f$ is isomorphic to the composite of those of $g$ and $f$ by the rebracketing $V\times_TT''\cong(V\times_TT')\times_{T'}T''$, which induces $c_{f,g}$. Hence [lem-sfb-eta-comp] gives exactly the composite coefficient map $\chi$ of the reconstruction lemma with this $\kappa$. Its composition clause identifies the direct-image comparison square with the specified underlying-sheaf compositor of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]. Clause (2) of the normalized-comparison lemma then identifies the pullback compositors of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp], which are their adjoint conjugates.

source.place: Steps 1–2, internal/sectionwise operation transport; assembly step 4 from the two extracted coherence statements.

proof.text: In the open square, Step 4 identifies $b:g\prime{}^*j^*\cong j\prime{}^*g^*$. Apply clause (3) of the normalized-comparison lemma with $J=j_!$, $U=j^*$, $J\prime=j\prime_!$, $U\prime=j\prime{}^*$, $P=g\prime{}^*$ and $Q=g^*$. Its displayed equality identifies the actual inverse mates, hence the stated open-extension base-change maps. Its invertibility equivalence gives the required implication. Finally Step 1 and the functor isomorphisms transport exactness of each operation by applying these exact equivalences and their inverses.
